newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks slip again, shrugging off U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks slip again, shrugging off U.S. data.

text.p: Swiss shares ended with a fifth consecutive slide on Thursday due mainly to fears of U.S. or German interest rate hikes, profit taking and technical and derivatives factors.
Dealers said U.S. data today including CPI were favourable and should have helped the market. "But the general feeling here is wait until this is over and buy later," one trader added.
Index heavyweights Roche, Novartis and UBS lost more than two percent each.
Further development was seen depending on Wall Street.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) lost 102.6 points or 1.81 percent to 5,579.5 points.
The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) slipped 45.05 points or 1.24 percent to 3,595.90.
Bourse volume stood at 2.94 billion Swiss francs.
Roche was due to release half-year results on Friday. Forecasts range from 2.05 to 2.75 billion Swiss francs.
SBC, which on Wednesday said first half bet profity grew a better-than-expected 84 percent, saw marginal losses. The stock fell 1.50 francs to 410 francs.
Merger partners Winterthur and Credit Suisse Group continued to post sizeable losses, pushed down by several downgrades and negative comments.
CS Group lost four francs to 186.25. Winterthur slid 44 francs to 1,372.
Individual stocks bucked the trend, including ABB, Surveillance, Sulzer and Ciba SC.
Dealers said ABB looked good from a technical point of view. The stock rose 17 francs to 2,304.
Sulzer, which climbed 19 francs to 1,219, was said to have been bolstered by a favourable study.
Swiss Life, which has posted impressive gains since its first trading day on July 3, was flat at 985.
